working_title: Lincolnshire's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Seacroft, North Shore, Woodhall Spa and the Coast
angle: Lincolnshire is routinely overlooked on the UK golf travel map, yet it offers a rare combination of proper championship links at Seacroft, a world-ranked inland heathland at Woodhall Spa, and a classic James Braid seaside layout at North Shore, all within comfortable driving distance of each other. The post makes the case for a two- or three-night circuit that mixes two completely different styles of golf (coastal links and heathland) in a county most golfers write off as flat and featureless.
research_notes:
- Seacroft Golf Club: traditional championship links founded 1895, located at the south end of Skegness adjacent to Gibraltar Point National Nature Reserve. Designed by Willie Fernie, par 71, approximately 6,492 yards. Out-and-back routing. Regularly rated in Top 100 courses in England. Sits on a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Fast-draining sandy soil makes it playable year-round. Described as 'the drier side of Britain' with below-average rainfall for England. Views across the Wash to the Norfolk coast. Advance booking required. Green fees: winter (Nov–Mar) midweek £35, weekend £50; summer (Apr–Oct) midweek £60, weekend £75 (figures from Visit Lincolnshire / club site — include as indicative only, advise readers to check current rates direct).
- Woodhall Spa Golf Club (Hotchkin Course): heathland course, home of England Golf and the National Golf Centre. Founded 1891. Par 73, 7,024 yards. Designed by Harry Vardon, modified significantly by H.S. Colt and S.V. Hotchkin; recent restoration by Renaissance Golf Design (trees felled, heather regenerated). Ranked in GOLF magazine's Top 100 Courses in the World (ranked 74th in 2025–26 edition). Third-highest-ranked inland course in Golf Monthly's UK & Ireland Top 100. Handicap limit applies (men 28, women 36). Visitors welcome every day; advance booking essential. Sand-based soil allows year-round play. Also has the Bracken Course (par 72, different character with more water) as a companion option. Located in Woodhall Spa village, approximately 19 miles east of Lincoln.
- North Shore Hotel & Golf Club, Skegness: James Braid design, founded 1910, par 71, 6,216 yards. Blends links and parkland holes; holes move in and out of dunes. Hotel sits within course grounds (36 bedrooms), making it a natural base for a golf break. Located 1km from Skegness town centre, alongside the North Sea. Member of the Association of James Braid Courses. Views over the Wash to Norfolk. Visitors welcome; green fees from £30 (check current rates direct).
- Sandilands Golf Club, Sutton-on-Sea: Lincolnshire's original links course, founded 1894. Lies alongside the beach with sea views from tees. Free-draining and relatively flat. Useful mention as an accessible, low-key addition to the circuit for groups with mixed abilities.
- Logistics: Woodhall Spa is inland, roughly 20–25 miles from Skegness coast. Lincoln is a natural gateway city with good road links (A158 connects Lincoln to the coast). The coastal strip is described as 'the drier side of Britain' making shoulder-season and winter trips viable. Seacroft and North Shore are very close to each other (both Skegness-area), so a coastal day pairing them is straightforward.
- Tone note: Lincolnshire is not glamorous in the way East Lothian or North Norfolk is — that's the point. The post should lean into the 'underrated' angle honestly, not oversell it.
